parts.text: Some students investigate an electrical circuit containing different combinations of resistors. They use circuit A shown in Fig. 2.1. Circuit A is not shown complete.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 2.1, complete circuit A to show a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference (p.d.) across resistor X and an ammeter connected to measure the current in the circuit. [2]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text:
either correct voltmeter symbol in parallel with X or correct ammeter symbol in series
second correct meter and circuit completed

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) A student measures the potential difference V across resistor X and the current I in the circuit. The voltmeter reading is shown in Fig. 2.2. The ammeter reading is shown in Fig. 2.3. Record, in the first line of Table 2.1, the values of V and I shown on the meters in Fig. 2.2 and Fig. 2.3. [1] Table 2.1 circuit V / I / R / Ω A B 2.1 0.54 C 1.6 0.39

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The student now connects two 5 Ω resistors in series between P and Q, as shown in Fig. 2.4, to form circuit B. The rest of the circuit remains as in Fig. 2.1. She measures the potential difference (p.d.) V across resistor X and the current I in the circuit. The student then connects three 5 Ω resistors in series between P and Q, as shown in Fig. 2.5, to form circuit C. The rest of the circuit remains as in Fig. 2.1. She measures the potential difference (p.d.) V across resistor X and the current I in the circuit. All her readings are shown in Table 2.1.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate, and record in Table 2.1, a value for the resistance R of resistor X for each combination of resistors the student has used. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation R = V I . [2]

ms.label: 2(c)(ii)
ms.text:
correct calculations of R (4.02 / ecf, 3.89, 4.10)
consistent 2 or consistent 3 sig figs

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
statement matching results
within limits of experimental accuracy / owtte
with values or comparative values seen

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) The results can be checked by using a different circuit. Draw, on Fig. 2.6, one other arrangement of three 5 Ω resistors between terminals P and Q. [1]

ms.label: 2(e)
ms.text: any parallel or series and parallel arrangement of three resistors

parts.label: i
parts.text: (f) (i) A student wants to determine R by using a variable resistor to vary the current in the circuit. Draw the circuit symbol for a variable resistor. [1]

ms.label: 2(f)(ii)
